what: Primerica sells term life insurance to middle-income North American families through a sales force of more than 150,000 part-time representatives, and also sells mutual funds and annuities.
customers: Middle-income households in the United States and Canada, visited at home by a local representative.
money: term policies sold by the representative force
mutual funds, annuities and managed accounts
moat: A sales force that recruits itself: representatives are mostly customers who became sellers, which gives Primerica distribution into a market large insurers cannot reach economically.
risks: Growth depends on recruiting and licensing new representatives, which is unpredictable
The business model draws periodic criticism and regulatory attention
Only six analysts cover the stock
opportunities: 11.4 times earnings and 9.4 times free cash flow with a 22.8% net margin
Revenue grew from $2.7B to $3.3B over four years
Policies stay in force for decades, and the investment products business grows with the same client base
watch: Life policies issued and the size of the licensed representative force.
